# Appeal of Denial — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**Governing Policy:** Aetna CPB 0660 - Knee Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html), last review 02/26/2026

**Member:** Rowan Carter
**Member ID:** W914903090
**Denial date:** 2026-08-19
**Reference number:** POC-5BA41AD17E-24277
**Payer/Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Missouri

---

Dear Aetna Appeals Review Team,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which was denied on 2026-08-19 with reference number POC-5BA41AD17E-24277 on the grounds that the procedure does not meet the plan's medical necessity criteria. I am asking Aetna to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the record shows that my case meets the plan's own published criteria for this surgery.

## The plan's criteria for unicompartmental knee arthroplasty

Aetna's own policy states:

> "unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is indicated when only 1 compartment is affected, and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is indicated when 2 or 3 compartments are affected."

My MRI from 2026-06-09 shows full-thickness cartilage loss with bone-on-bone apposition in the medial compartment, with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. The imaging findings in my record describe involvement of the medial compartment only; no other compartment is documented as affected. This is the situation the policy describes as appropriate for UKA rather than TKA.

The policy also states that:

> "Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty using Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved devices is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral), and who meet the following criteria (see also Additional Note ):"

My MRI findings of full-thickness, bone-on-bone cartilage loss with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes are, in my understanding, consistent with advanced osteoarthritis affecting a single compartment, as described here.

## Conservative therapy already completed

The plan's policy states:

> "Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication) - with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year, including all of the following, unless contraindicated:"

My physical therapy discharge note documents 14 weeks of supervised, in-person physical therapy (16 visits) from 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-17, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion. In addition, my record documents 8 months of NSAID use with inadequate relief and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-17 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief. This is a documented history of the kind of non-surgical management the policy describes:

> "and History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management;"

## Severity of my condition

The policy also recognizes that:

> "Conservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint (medial and/or lateral but not patello-femoral) or severe angular deformity, or for avascular necrosis with collapse of tibial or femoral condyle, or progressive flexion contracture."

My MRI documents bone-on-bone apposition in the medial, weight-bearing compartment of my knee. I have already completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy, 8 months of NSAID use, and a corticosteroid injection, despite the severity described above, and I continue to have significant pain and functional limitation. My record documents that I cannot climb stairs without assistance and wake 3-4 times nightly due to pain, along with positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion on exam.

## Request

Based on the plan's own criteria and the documentation in my medical record, I am asking Aetna to reverse this denial and approve coverage for CPT 27446 as recommended by my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-15, and that the appeal address on my denial letter is authoritative; I am also submitting this through Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form as instructed, and I have noted the fax number 859-425-3379 as a backup option.

Please let me know if any additional records or information are needed to complete this review.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

Rowan Carter
Member ID: W914903090
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Date of signature]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
